newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees rising Mexican oilseeds imports.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees rising Mexican oilseeds imports.

text.p: Mexico should import 2.63 million tonnes of soybeans in the 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) season, up from 2.38 million in 95/96, the Oil World newsletter said.

The independent publication also forecast Mexico's soy oil purchases abroad in 96/97 at 80,000 tonnes compared with 53,000 tonnes in the previous season and palm oil imports at 110,000 tonnes (88,000).

Domestic oilseeds production in 96/97 was put slightly higher at 730,000 tonnes from a little changed 600,000 hectare area, but well down from levels seen in the early 1990s and not keeping pace with industrial demand.
Mexico's higher soybean imports would partly replace lower rapeseed purchases from tight global markets, Oil World said, putting rape imports at 450,000 tonnes (683,000 in 95/96).
Mexico's total oils and fats imports were pegged at 965,000 tonnes in 1996/97 (versus 925,000 previously), which included sun oil at 285,000 tonnes (304,000 previously).

The country's oilmeal imports in 96/97 were estimated at 620,000 tonnes, up from 600,000 in 95/96, but higher domestic demand would mostly be met via the crushing of imported soybeans, Oil World added.
